title: bug: JetBrains protected selection reads a stored PROTECTED pin as ABSENT when the IDE state store root's real path is on a drive letter the lookup cannot place (residual of 1c2bfeca)
description:
Reported 2026-10-30 19:35Z by worker-73c29a03 (#general msg-34e57211, msg-7d395a68), from reading 1c2bfeca's landed code (7eec5dbe, DONE 19:29:53Z). It is untested so far. Routed by the governor to its own row.

Mechanism, as landed in moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/util/RuntimeSelectionPolicy.kt:
- storedProfile (:86-88) reads the pin when `usableFor(basePath) || windowsHost && listOf(store.root, basePath).any(::unprovableDrive)`.
- That disjunct tests the store root and the base only as written, never their real paths.
- Suppose the store root is written on a drive that resolves, but its real path, through a junction or symlink, lies on a letter whose mapping the lookup cannot place, such as an ImDisk volume (\Device\ImDisk0), a null mapping or a throwing query.
- Then outsideByIdentity returns false (:446/:448), usableFor is false, and the disjunct is false. A previously persisted PROTECTED pin reads ABSENT, and selection becomes LEGACY with no downgrade ask.
- Before 1c2bfeca that pin was honored. This is the class of 1c2bfeca's REPRO 1 (governor comment-2be9b525: fail closed, never drop an existing external PROTECTED pin), with a narrower trigger.

Split of ownership:
- The BASE side (the base's real path) belongs to task-52fb6178: its refusal 2 routes into the unprovable read (architect-bc59d28a's addendum).
- This row owns the STORE-ROOT side only.
- If 52fb6178's landed predicate already covers the store root's real path, this row delivers the regression test and says so.

Keep: a provably-inside store (D2, runIde sandbox) still reads ABSENT. persist() still requires a provably-outside store. A read under an unprovable store may only add PROTECTED and the ask. Never write under an unprovable store.
definitionOfDone: On a Windows host, when the IDE state store root is written on a drive that resolves but its real path (junction or symlink) lies on a drive letter whose mapping the lookup cannot place (e.g. \Device\ImDisk0, null, or a throwing windowsDriveTarget), a previously persisted PROTECTED pin is still honored: profile() returns PROTECTED, requests the downgrade confirmation, and the stored record is unchanged. Shown by a new JetBrains unit test with an injected windowsDriveTarget; the completion summary states whether it was RED on the row's parent commit.

Unchanged behavior elsewhere: a provably-inside store still reads ABSENT (D2), a provably-outside store behaves as before, no write happens under an unprovable store, and the existing RuntimeSelectionPolicyTest and MoeDaemonSupervisorTest cases pass unchanged.

cd moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew test exits 0 (from WSL: cmd.exe /d /c "set GRADLE_OPTS=-Xmx512m&& cd /d D:\projexts\moes\moe-jetbrains && .\gradlew.bat test --rerun") under the jetbrains-gradle lease, with output supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: Scope: RuntimeSelectionPolicy.kt's stored-profile read predicate (and a shared helper it calls) plus RuntimeSelectionPolicyTest.kt. ProtectedStateStore, the record format, persist(), projectKey and alias-spelling records (task-9a1da6f6) stay unchanged.

08bb7723 scope (governor routing, 2026-10-30 19:50Z): beyond DoD 1's store-root case, this row also owns the BASE-side failed physical proof. Example: a base on a subst drive S: -> C:\t where C:\t is a junction to a volume the lookup cannot place (e.g. ImDisk). The base's real path S:\x is plain, so 52fb6178's unplainBase is false, but physicalProject(real) == null. That case must also read the stored pin: profile() returns PROTECTED plus the downgrade ask, the record is unchanged, and nothing is written. Prove it with a test using the same injected/cross-volume junction fixture as DoD 1, held to DoD 1's standard. QA treats this case as in scope and required, not as scope creep. DoD 2 and 3 apply unchanged.

implementationPlan.description:
Tests first. File: moe-jetbrains/src/test/kotlin/com/moe/util/RuntimeSelectionPolicyTest.kt.

Re-read it and RuntimeSelectionPolicy.kt as 52fb6178 landed them. This row dependsOn that one, whose N13, N14 and S10-S12 rows are in this file. Keep every existing row byte-identical.

Add D10, D11 and D12 directly after D9, plus one private helper beside withDriveTargets.
- Each row starts with assumeTrue(..., RuntimeSelectionPolicy.windowsHost) and must RUN on the verification host.
- Reuse withProfileStore, withSubst, withDriveTargets, junction, volumeSpelling, profileJson, writeProfile, writeProjectJson, project, storeFiles and realFile.
- Paths below are runtime spellings: double the backslashes in Kotlin.
- Label every assertion with its case and answer index.

Why D10 needs two subst drives:
- A junction's real path always lands on the physical volume's letter.
- toRealPath keeps a subst letter unless it crosses a reparse point.
So the store or project is spelled on a subst drive z, which a fake places as a whole local volume. The junction's own drive is faked unplaceable, as an ImDisk RAM disk would be.

D10 `D10 a protected pin survives a restart on which a junction leads the store or the project onto a drive no mapping can place`. It runs in withProfileStore { _, dir, asks -> }, where dir declares verified-local.

Setup:
- stores = temporaryFolder.newFolder("stores");
- link = File(temporaryFolder.root, "system-link"), then assertTrue(junction(link.toPath(), stores.toPath()));
- far = File(stores, "proj"), with a verified-local project.json;
- temporaryFolder.newFolder("state");
- fresh = project(legacy);
- physical = realFile(stores).path.substring(0, 2).uppercase();
- native = RuntimeSelectionPolicy.windowsDriveTarget.
Then run withSubst(temporaryFolder.root) { z -> withSubst(link) { y -> ... } }. y's root IS the junction, so toRealPath keeps y:.

With near = "$z\<dir.name>", the cases (label, base, store) are:
1. store through a junction: near, ProtectedStateStore("$z\system-link\moe\protected-state"). This is DoD 1.
2. store on a drive rooted at a junction: near, ProtectedStateStore("$y\moe\protected-state").
3. project on a drive rooted at a junction: "$y\proj", ProtectedStateStore("$z\state\moe\protected-state"). This is rail prop-a89f8112's base case: unplainBase is false, and physicalProject(real) is null.

Persist with native mappings. For each case:
- install the store and call forgetSessionForTest();
- assertEquals(PROTECTED, profile(base)), which persists the pin;
- assertTrue(store.usableFor(base));
- assertEquals(profileJson(File(base), "protected"), store.read(profileRecordName(base))).
Then:
- write a sandbox store at "$near\build\idea-sandbox\system\moe\protected-state" holding near's record directly, with store.write;
- writeProfile legacy for dir and for far.

Restart with the fake. The junction's drive gets each answer in turn: { "\Device\ImDisk0" }, { null }, { throw IllegalStateException("native") }, { throw UnsatisfiedLinkError("jnidispatch") }.
For each, run withDriveTargets({ when (it) { z -> "\Device\HarddiskVolume1"; y -> "\??\$z\system-link"; physical -> answer(it); else -> native(it) } }).
Comment: z stands for a drive the lookup places, and physical for one it cannot. y expands through z and names the same folder as its native mapping.

Inside, for each case:
- assertFalse(store.usableFor(base));
- install the store, call forgetSessionForTest(), and assertEquals(PROTECTED, profile(base));
- assertEquals(base, asks.paths.last());
- call asks.answers.last()(true);
- the record still equals profileJson(File(base), "protected"), and storeFiles(store) is exactly [its name].

Then, still under the fake:
- with case 1's store installed, profile("$z\<fresh.name>") is LEGACY, with no ask;
- with the sandbox installed and forgetSessionForTest(), profile(near) is LEGACY, with no ask. On a placed drive the sandbox is provably inside (D2).
After the loop, asks.paths has exactly 12 entries.

D11 `D11 a protected pin survives a restart on which the store is spelled without a drive`. It runs in withProfileStore { store, dir, asks -> }.
- profileOf(dir) persists PROTECTED through the drive spelling.
- device = volumeSpelling(store.root.toFile()), then assumeTrue("mountvol names the volume", device != null).
- deviceStore = ProtectedStateStore(Paths.get(device)), then writeProfile(dir, "legacy").
Assert:
- assertFalse(deviceStore.usableFor(dir.path));
- with deviceStore installed and forgetSessionForTest(), profile is PROTECTED and asks.paths == [dir.path];
- after the answer true, store.read(name) and storeFiles(store) are unchanged.
Control: a fresh legacy project reads LEGACY, with no ask.

D12 `D12 a protected pin survives a restart on which the store or the project has no real path`.

Helper withUnlistable(dir: File, body):
- prepend an ACL DENY entry for the owner, with AclEntryPermission.LIST_DIRECTORY, on dir;
- run body;
- restore the previous ACL in finally.
KDoc: toRealPath lists each folder on the way, so it fails below dir. Opening a known path still works, because traverse checking is bypassed. This is what happens with a junction onto a volume Windows cannot name, such as an ImDisk RAM disk outside the mount manager.

The row runs in withProfileStore { store, dir, asks -> }, with the native seam. Write every record directly while unlocked. Cases:
1. store below an unlistable folder: base dir.path, locked = newFolder("locked-store"), and the store at locked\moe\protected-state.
2. project below an unlistable folder: base = realFile(<newFolder("locked-project")>\proj).path, which has a legacy project.json; the store is withProfileStore's store. Use the real spelling: under the deny, projectKey falls back to the spelling, which must equal the record's key.

For each case:
- compute name and record before locking;
- inside withUnlistable(locked), assertFalse(store.usableFor(base)). This also proves the deny took effect;
- install the store, call forgetSessionForTest(), and assert PROTECTED;
- the ask names base;
- after the answer true, record and storeFiles are unchanged.

2. Acquire jetbrains-gradle, then copy the rows in.
3. Run: cmd.exe /d /c "set GRADLE_OPTS=-Xmx512m&& cd /d D:\projexts\moes\moe-jetbrains && .\gradlew.bat test --rerun --tests com.moe.util.RuntimeSelectionPolicyTest"

5. Keep the lease and go straight to step 2, so no peer's gate compiles your red rows (mem:gotcha-jetbrains-shared-tree-gate-peer-red).
If a case passes on the parent, 52fb6178 already covers it: name it. If every case passes, step 2 makes no production change and proves the rows with mutant M1 instead.

implementationPlan.description:
Production. File: moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/util/RuntimeSelectionPolicy.kt. Still under step 1's lease.

(a) Extract outsideByIdentity's placement walk into a new private helper beside it: private fun physicalFolder(path: Path): Path?. Use a block body, never a return inside an expression body.
- Start from Paths.get(resolveWindowsDrivePath(path.toString()) ?: return null).
- Walk to the nearest existing folder with toRealPath. A NoSuchFileException moves to the parent.
- Return real?.let(::physicalPath).
Error handling: catch Exception and IOError and return null, so physicalFolder never throws. A failed resolution means unplaceable, which reads the pin; it never means absent. resolveWindowsDrivePath already turns a failed, null or LinkageError lookup into null.
KDoc:
- It returns [path]'s nearest existing folder, as file identity compares it.
- It returns null when a drive on the way cannot be proved local, a resolution fails, or nothing on the way exists.
- It asks the drive lookup before NIO opens anything, so nothing is opened through a drive its spelling cannot place.
outsideByIdentity keeps its signature, the project == null check, the isSameFile walk, `proved` and both catches. It starts from physicalFolder(path), and its answers do not change. Point its KDoc at physicalFolder.

(b) storedProfile's Windows-only read disjunct.
At plan time it is `windowsHost && (unprovableDrive(it.root.toString()) || unplainBase(basePath))`, which is 52fb6178's approved shape (comment-0c896da0).
Make it `windowsHost && (physicalFolder(it.root) == null || unplainBase(basePath) || physicalFolder(Paths.get(basePath)) == null)`.
- physicalFolder(it.root) replaces unprovableDrive(it.root.toString()). Its first step is the same lookup, so it covers everything that term did. It adds a junction, link or subst that leads onto a drive the lookup cannot place, a real path that cannot be found, and a spelling with no drive.
- The base's physical folder comes last. unplainBase runs its raw spelling check first, so Paths.get never sees a base that check refuses (JDK 17 throws on a trailing space), and a non-plain base is never opened.
- A missing base still reads ABSENT, because physicalFolder defers it to its parent.
- An existing base whose toRealPath fails now reads the pin. That answers the governor's comment-3696e987.
- If 52fb6178 landed another shape, keep its base terms byte-identical. Swap only a root term that is exactly unprovableDrive(it.root.toString()); otherwise OR the new terms after its own.
Update the comment above the predicate. The pin is also read when the store root or the base has no physical folder:
- a drive mapping that cannot place it, as written or through a junction, link or subst;
- a real path that cannot be found;
- no drive at all.
A missing base reads as absent. Writes still need a store provably outside the project.
storedProfile's existing catch is unchanged: a failed read is UNTRUSTED, which is PROTECTED.

Do not change any of these: persist(), usableStore, verifiedFromStore, remember, save, load, ProtectedStateStore, projectKey, the record format, physicalPath, physicalProject, resolveWindowsDrivePath, unprovableDrive, isOutsideProject, select, or 52fb6178's helpers.

(c) Mutants. Run each under the same lease, with step 1's targeted command. Back up the file outside the repo, write the mutant, run it, restore the file, and check its sha256 (mem:pattern-qa-mutation-red-under-gradle-lease).
- M2, first-letter checks only. The root term becomes `unprovableDrive(it.root.toString()) || realPathOrNull(it.root.toString())?.let { unprovableDrive(it.toString()) } == true`, with no base physical-folder term. Expect D10 cases 2 and 3, D11, and both D12 cases to fail.
- M3. The root term becomes `true`. Expect D10's sandbox (D2) assertion to fail.
- M1, only if step 1 found every case GREEN on the parent. The root term becomes 1c2bfeca's unprovableDrive(it.root.toString()), with no base physical-folder term. Expect the D10 cases to fail.

(d) GREEN. The targeted run passes with D10, D11 and D12 executed. Then release the lease.
The step note records:

- what each mutant failed;
- the GREEN count.

comments.content:
FYI from task-52fb6178 (worker-e60b90bd), now going to REVIEW. It names one more store-root case on this row's side. 52fb did not widen for it, per the planner note on 52fb.

52fb's isPlainLocalPath now refuses any segment that ends in '.' or ' '. usableFor(base) passes the store root as the candidate. So a store root whose spelling has such a segment now makes usableFor false; examples are a custom idea.system.path like `D:\idea.`, or a junction onto `X:\state.` (its real path). For a plain base, the read gate's other two disjuncts are false as well: unprovableDrive(root) and unplainBase(base). So a PROTECTED pin stored there earlier now reads ABSENT.

Before 52fb that store was usable, because Win32 drops the trailing dot when it opens the path. The case is contrived.

52fb's unplainBase judges only the base. unprovableDrive(root) still reads the root only as written. If your read predicate treats a root whose spelling or real path is not plain as "unprovable", it covers this case as well. Otherwise, please list it as a residual.

acceptanceCriteria: D10, on Windows. Fakes: subst z answers \Device\HarddiskVolume1; subst y, rooted at a junction, expands through z; the junction's drive answers \Device\ImDisk0, null, IllegalStateException or UnsatisfiedLinkError. Three cases: a store spelled through the junction (DoD 1), a store on y, and a project on y with a placeable store (rail prop-a89f8112). In each, a restart with a legacy declaration gives profile(base) == PROTECTED and one ask naming base. After Allow, the record and the store's file list are unchanged, and usableFor(base) is false. With native mappings, all three stores are usable and the pins persist.

D10 controls, under the same fake: a fresh legacy project reads LEGACY without an ask through the unplaceable store, and a sandbox store under the project on z, holding the same PROTECTED record, reads LEGACY without an ask.

Chosen: one question for both sides, physicalFolder(path) == null. It is extracted from outsideByIdentity, so storedProfile reads exactly when identity could not place the store root or the base. It covers:
- the DoD case;
- the rail's base case, a subst rooted at a junction;

- a spelling with no drive.
Rejected:
- First-letter checks on the real path, which is 52fb6178's unplainBase shape applied to the root. They miss a subst rooted at a junction, because toRealPath keeps the letter, and they miss a real path that cannot be found. M2 pins the difference.
- Reading whenever usableFor is false. That reads a provably-inside sandbox (D2). M3 pins it.
- realPathOrNull(base)?.let(::physicalProject) == null for the base. It would also read a missing base; physicalFolder defers a missing base to its parent, so it stays ABSENT.
- A tri-state isOutsideProject. It touches selection and every caller.
- A store-only copy of the walk. That is the same logic twice.
- Recording ABSENT as safe for an existing base whose toRealPath fails (comment-3696e987's alternative). That case is a LEGACY downgrade with no ask, and it is the realistic ImDisk outcome.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- The 'unprovable' read is storedProfile's Windows-only disjunct, after usableFor. 52fb6178 adds unplainBase to it (the approved shape, comment-0c896da0). This row adds the physical-folder terms.
- outsideByIdentity's false conflates 'proved inside' with 'could not place'. physicalFolder == null is exactly the second.
- physicalFolder(root) subsumes unprovableDrive(root): it makes the same lookup first, and opens nothing before it.
- A fake that answers a subst letter with \Device\HarddiskVolume1 makes resolveWindowsDrivePath treat that letter as a whole volume. That is how a one-drive host models a store written on a drive that resolves.
- toRealPath copies the root component without FindFirstFile. So a subst whose root is the junction (withSubst(link), as in N9) keeps its letter, and only expansion reaches the junction.
- Denying the owner LIST_DIRECTORY on a folder makes toRealPath fail below it. Direct opens (GetFileAttributesEx, CreateFile) still work, because traverse checking is bypassed.
- withProfileStore resets the policy in finally, and withSubst removes only its own drive. TemporaryFolder deletes through junctions, as N9 shows.
